Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Australia Women's reply. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Phoebe Litchfield and Georgia Voll walk in to open for Australia Women. Sayali Satghare has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Pink ball under the lights - With a first innings total of 198 on the board, the focus now shifts to the Indian bowlers. The pink ball is famously the most lethal during the twilight and night sessions, and India Women will be eager to exploit the same movement and bounce that troubled them. With the conditions now perfectly suited for swing and seam, the Indian pace attack must make early inroads to stay in the hunt. All eyes are on the WACA deck to see how the Australian openers respond to the challenge under the glow of the floodlights.

Sutherland led the Australian charge - Australia’s bowling performance was nothing short of professional. Annabel Sutherland was the standout performer, finishing as the pick of the bowlers with four wickets, consistently hitting uncomfortable lengths for the Indian batters. She was brilliantly supported by debutant Lucy Hamilton, who capped off a dream start to her Test career with three wickets. Darcie Brown chipped in with two scalps, and Ashleigh Gardner claimed one, rounding out a dominant display by the Aussies with the ball.

Jemimah and Kashvee provide resistance - Despite the collapse, there were moments of individual brilliance. Jemimah Rodrigues stood tall amidst the ruins, playing a composed and technically sound innings to bring up a vital half-century. Her resilience was matched late in the day by debutant Kashvee Gautam, who showed immense grit in her first Test outing. Gautam remained unbeaten on 34, proving her worth with the bat and ensuring India at least pushed around the 200-mark. Their efforts provided a glimmer of hope for a side that found itself under the pump for most of the day.

India’s batting order falters - The Indian first innings concluded much sooner than the visitors or their fans had hoped, as they were bundled out for 198 in the final session on Day 1. After being put in to bat on a challenging WACA surface, India struggled to find stability, losing Smriti Mandhana early and failing to build substantial partnerships. While Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Harmanpreet Kaur, and Richa Ghosh all managed to get starts, none could convert them into the big scores required to anchor the innings. The middle order’s inability to weather the Australian storm left India searching for answers as wickets fell at regular intervals.

OUT! TAKEN! Darcie Brown wraps up the India Women's innings. Bangs it short, outside off, Kranti Gaud stays back and looks to pull it but gets a top edge. The ball goes over the keeper. Annabel Sutherland moves back from first slip and takes a magnificent low catch. Top performance from the Aussies with the ball. India Women have been bowled out for 198 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of Day 1. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Sayali Satghare and Kashvee Gautam will resume their innings. Annabel Sutherland will start with the ball. Let's go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Two down, one more to go - The first two sessions on Day 1 of this 'Pink Ball' Test have flown by. The next session should be interesting as the artificial lights will be in full effect. India Women are still hanging around, looking to get to 200 and then some. The Aussies will be eager to wrap things quickly after the break and get out to bat. Stay tuned as the final session is coming up at 3.52 pm IST (10.22 am GMT).

Let's now hear from Annabel Sutherland - Sutherland acknowledges the fact that opportunities to play with the pink ball are rare, but the ball continues to shape and move significantly in the current conditions. She notes that plenty is happening when the ball lands in the right areas and emphasizes that the Australian attack remains determined to capitalize on this movement to claim the remaining wickets as quickly as possible.

Falling behind in the game - There has been some resistance from India Women in the second session on Day 1, but the top order just didn't do enough early on. Jemimah Rodrigues did score a half-century and Richa Ghosh also got a start, but it is Kashvee Gautam who is keeping the fight alive right now. Sayali Satghare is alongside Gautam and both of them can certainly bat. However, India will need something special from these two to get to a decent total.

Time for a Dinner break - SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 85 runs, and 4 wickets. Another session that has been dominated by the Aussies. Annabel Sutherland has been the star of the show so far but Lucy Hamilton is having a debut to remember as well, with 3 wickets to her name just like Sutherland. Australia Women will feel they should have bundled out India by now but won't be too displeased heading into the night session.

A lot relying on Jemimah and Deepti - The focus now shifts to Jemimah Rodrigues, who has looked solid and determined, and the experienced Deepti Sharma. The Indian dugout will be banking on this duo to stabilize the innings and navigate the majority of the second session. This period is expected to be the best time for batting before the twilight hours arrive and the pink ball begins to zip around under the floodlights. If India can bat through the next two hours without further damage, they may yet claw their way back into the contest. The action resumes for the second session at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT).

Debutant Lucy - Australian debutant Lucy Hamilton expresses her immense excitement and thrill at securing her first Test wicket. She describes receiving her baggy green from Beth Mooney as a really special moment and feels a deep sense of pride running out with the team. Maintaining a focused approach, she notes that the Australian side plans to keep the pressure on the Indian batters by consistently hitting a hard line and length. Hamilton also acknowledges the heartwarming support she has received from fans across the country, noting that seeing her family in the stands brings a genuine smile to her face.

India’s top order struggles - After being asked to bat, India reached tea at 99/4, struggling to convert promising starts into substantial scores. While Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, and Harmanpreet Kaur all looked comfortable briefly, they were unable to navigate the disciplined lines set by the Australian pacers. The loss of four wickets in the opening session puts the visitors on the back foot, especially given that the ball is bound to swing more under the lights and when the breeze will start to kick-in.

Australia’s pace battery fires early - Australia’s decision to bowl first is paying dividends as their fast bowling cartel has kept the Indian batters under relentless pressure. Debutant Lucy Hamilton enjoyed a dream start to her Test career, claiming the massive wicket of Smriti Mandhana as her maiden scalp. The clinical Annabel Sutherland further dented the visitors' progress by picking up two crucial wickets, while Darcie Brown produced a peach of a delivery to dismiss the Indian captain, Harmanpreet Kaur. The disciplined Australian attack has ensured that runs are hard to come by, heading into the break with significant momentum.

Australia asserts early control - The opening session of this historic pink-ball Test concludes with Australia firmly in the driver’s seat, leaving India at 99 for 4 as the players head for Tea. Despite promising starts from Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, and Harmanpreet Kaur, the visitors struggled to build momentum against a relentless Australian attack.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with an emphatic pre-match ceremony and now the action shifts to the action. Alyssa Healy leads Australia Women out in the middle with the players taking their respective field positions. Shafali Verma partners with Smriti Mandhana at the top for India Women. Darcie Brown will be bowling the first over for Australia Women.

We are all set for the pre-match formalities. Both sides have lined up on either side of the match officials. Harmanpreet Kaur leads India Women while Alyssa Healy leads Australia Women out in the middle for their respective national anthems. It will be India's first, followed by that of Australia.

Early movement on offer, says Martin - In her pitch analysis, Katey Martin highlights the searingly hot conditions at the WACA, with temperatures set to soar to 38 degrees, making the heat as much of a factor as the wicket itself. She observes a healthy green tinge and thick grass coverage, suggesting the pink ball may offer genuine sideways movement and hold in the surface during the opening stages. Martin concludes by saying that if the openers survive the first two hours of play, they might eye a big one on this deck as Day 2 and Day 3 will be the best for batting.

Indian captain - Harmanpreet Kaur admits she also preferred to bowl first but maintains that her side must excel regardless of the toss to overcome their recent ODI struggles. She emphasizes the need to play their best cricket to secure a win and reveals a balanced lineup with four debutants, three pacers, and two spinners.

Australian captain - Alyssa Healy opts to bowl first, acknowledging that while the surface looks inviting for batters, she is eager to see what her young, exciting fast bowling cartel can extract from the pitch early on. Although she hasn't fully processed the emotion of her final Test match, she remains focused on the four days of competitive cricket ahead while thanking her friends and family for their overwhelming support. Regarding the lineup, she confirms that Lucy Hamilton makes her debut after an impressive week, and Ellyse Perry has recovered sufficiently to take her place at number three.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal (on Debut), Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Kashvee Gautam (on Debut), Sneh Rana, Sayali Satghare (on Debut), Kranti Gaud (on Debut).

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Phoebe Litchfield, Georgia Voll, Ellyse Perry, Alyssa Healy (C), Annabel Sutherland, Beth Mooney (WK), Ashleigh Gardner, Tahlia McGrath, Alana King, Lucy Hamilton (on Debut), Darcie Brown.
TOSS - Australia Women have won the coin flip and will be BOWLING first​​​​​​.

A battle of legacy and grit - As only the fourth Day-Night Test in women's history, this game represents the pinnacle of the sport. Australia aims to assert their home dominance and give their captain a golden farewell, while India seeks to prove that their Mumbai triumph was no fluke. Expect a contest where momentum swings with the setting sun, and where the winner will be the side that best tames the bounce of the WACA and the unpredictability of the pink ball. Stay tuned as toss and team news are not far from us.

India’s resilience and the youthful charge - India Women enter this contest with the confidence of having defeated Australia in their last red-ball encounter at the Wankhede in 2023. However, the bouncy Perth deck is a different beast. With pace spearhead Renuka Singh Thakur out due to workload management, all eyes are on 22-year-old debutant Kashvee Gautam. The batting rests on the elegant shoulders of Smriti Mandhana and the explosive Shafali Verma, while skipper Harmanpreet Kaur looks to carry her fine ODI form into the longest format. With a lot of uncapped Test players in the squad, India is going big on fresh energy to script their first-ever away Test win against the Aussies.

Healy’s final bow - This match is draped in emotion as it marks the final international appearance for Australian legend Alyssa Healy. To honour her 299-match career, Cricket Australia has renamed the WACA hill 'Healy Hill' for this Test. Australia's squad remains formidable despite injuries. The inclusion of heavyweights like Beth Mooney and the potentially batter-only Ellyse Perry ensures their lineup remains the one to beat. Tahlia McGrath and Annabel Sutherland remain the absolute key for the Australian side with both bat and ball to provide the balance they need on a deck that might just help the seamers as the sun sets.

The quest for the series draw - The stakes couldn't be higher for the visitors as Australia currently holds a commanding 8-4 lead in the multi-format points table following a dominant 3-0 sweep in the ODIs. India Women arrive at the WACA needing a win to bring the series to an 8-8 deadlock. Even if India secures this historic victory, Australia will retain the trophy by virtue of their 2021 series win, but for Harmanpreet Kaur’s side, drawing level on points in Australian conditions would be a massive statement of intent.

Showdown at the WACA - Welcome to cricket fans everywhere as we gather at Perth’s iconic WACA Ground, where the atmospheric glow of the floodlights and the unpredictable pink ball set a dramatic stage for this monumental one-off Day-Night Test between Australia Women and India Women.
